rationale: bugs_open/040-kafka-dial, the behaviour round - deliberately SEPARATE from the instrumentation round (correlation a414d81b) because this case's round 1 was vetoed for bundling the two. A census, not a hunch: MEASURED 2026-08-21 over agent_error_log's retained window, 63 rows matching 'Kafka write error' plus 40 matching 'has no leader', across 93 DISTINCT ORCHESTRATIONS, recurring most days since 08-10. The worst shape is a workflow whose every substantive step has already committed failing at its terminal complete_workflow send: the work is done and the head row reads FAILED. Two independent reasons it is not self-correcting. kafka-go will not retry it - its writer breaks after ONE attempt on !isTemporary, and protocol.ErrNoLeader is a bare string type with no Temporary() method, which is the observed 'Kafka write errors (1/1)' fingerprint. And platform/errors' nine transient needles match NEITHER string, so every one of those 103 rows classified error_unrecoverable and terminated work permanently on a condition usually over in seconds. This round adds a bounded retry, OPT-IN with the unsafe side OFF and adopted at four named sites, and admits exactly two needles - refusing a third that would reclassify permanent failures as retryable.

plan.summary: Add a bounded, jittered, opt-in produce retry (ProduceWithRetry, and WithRetry as a variadic DeliverOption on DeliverReply) that never retries deterministic errors and returns the last attempt's error verbatim; adopt it at the four reply/terminal sites where a lost send costs finished work; and admit two transient needles so a residual failure is redispatchable rather than terminal. The five other DeliverReply callers are byte-identical to today, pinned by a test.

edits.rationale: The retry itself. Bounded (4 attempts, ~44s worst case stated in the doc comment) and jittered, because these failures are CORRELATED - a leadership election fails every producer in the fleet at once and an unjittered backoff marches them all back onto the broker in the same instant. Deterministic errors are never retried: validation refusal (bugs_open/274 - the headers are wrong by construction), too-large (the broker's limit does not move, and DeliverReply's remedy for it is to DEGRADE, which stays its own), and context-cancelled (nobody is left to answer). The last attempt's error is returned VERBATIM, which is load-bearing rather than tidiness: every caller wraps it in its own message and platform/errors' classifier matches needles inside them, so a wrapping layer here would silently change what all of that sees. A recoveries counter is added in the same file's service because a falling failure count cannot distinguish 'the fix worked' from 'the weather was quiet' - this counter can.

Variadic DeliverOption so the FIVE existing callers compile and behave UNCHANGED - agentbase, orchestration/helpers, coordinator, webscrape adapter, batch_handler. With no options, send is one ProduceWithValidation call, byte for byte what this function did before. The degrade path routes through the same send, so a degraded resend gets the policy too, while the ORIGINAL oversize send is never retried (too-large is deterministic). The function's own comment 'the caller's existing retry path stays in charge' is qualified at source: it was TRUE and it named a caller that does not exist on the complete_workflow path, where the caller is failWorkflow and it has no retry.

Adopter 1, and the site the census is mostly about. This is the terminal step: every substantive result is already committed and this send is the only thing between a finished workflow and a head row that reads FAILED. Safe to retry - extractFinalResult, extractReplyToMetadata and buildResponseMessage above it are pure reads of CollectedData - and a duplicate reply from a lost ack is absorbed by the parent's two-phase ClaimAwaitedRequest. The 'failed to send response: %w' wrapper is untouched.

Adopters 2 and 3, and they close a real asymmetry: notifyParentOfSuccess has gone through the shared DeliverReply seam since bugs_open/133, while notifyParentOfFailure stayed a bare fire-once log-and-drop. If that send fails the parent learns nothing and waits out its own timeout, which is exactly the case worth resending. The last-resort log stays - there is no one left to tell - but it now retried first. notifyParentOfSuccess gains WithRetry on its existing call, one line.

edits.rationale: Two needles, admitted on the census above and each argued in the file's own convention. 'kafka write error' (singular, matching 'Kafka write errors (1/1)' as a prefix) and 'no leader' rather than the full 'topic partition has no leader' - because kafka.WriteErrors' Error() embeds its members' texts, so the composite that actually arrives is matched by the shorter form and the longer one would miss it. DELIBERATELY REFUSED, and this is the load-bearing half: 'write message to kafka'. It is our own producer's wrapper on EVERY write failure, including the deterministic oversize refusal and the validation refusal, so admitting it would reclassify permanent failures as retryable - precisely the bugs_open/274 defect that spent 12 days being reported as 'try again'. The two admitted needles cover all 103 measured rows without it, and a control test asserts both deterministic refusals still classify TERMINAL.

edits.rationale: Mutation-proven, with two results recorded honestly rather than asserted. FIRST, a test caught a REAL DEFECT in my own code: the jitter was rand.Int63n(delay)+delay/2, which spans [delay/2, 1.5*delay) and therefore BREAKS MaxDelay by up to 50% - MaxDelay is a bound or it is decoration. SECOND, an honest negative: the default-OFF pin does NOT discriminate the cfg.retry flag. Removing that check alone survives, because the zero-value RetryPolicy's Attempts of 0 is clamped to 1 - two mechanisms in series. That is a real belt-and-braces property; the test pins the OBSERVABLE promise ('no option, one attempt') which is what the five existing callers depend on, the clamp is pinned separately, and the mutation that DOES fail it (defaulting retry:true WITH a non-zero policy) is named in the test and was applied to confirm it. Also pinned: deterministic errors stop the loop at one call; the degrade path is undisturbed; a cancelled context returns the PRODUCE error not the context error; and the error-text contract.

grounded_in: MEASURED 2026-08-21, live agent_error_log over its retained window 2026-07-22..08-21: 63 rows matching 'Kafka write error', 40 matching 'has no leader', 93 distinct orchestration_ids; per-day 08-10:3, 08-11:14, 08-12:2, 08-14:14, 08-15:16, 08-18:8, 08-20:3; steps hit include complete/complete_workflow 11, process_message 10, orchestrate 9, plus ~20 call_agent dispatch steps.
kafka-go v0.4.47 writer.go: 'if !isTemporary(err) && !isTransientNetworkError(err) { break }' inside the MaxAttempts loop - so the loop is not the retry it appears to be for a non-Temporary error.

kafka-go v0.4.47 protocol/error.go: 'ErrNoLeader Error = "topic partition has no leader"' with 'func (e Error) Error() string' as the type's only method - no Temporary(), hence one attempt, hence the '(1/1)' in the live error text.

platform/errors/transient_failure.go before this change - the nine needles 'deadline exceeded, timeout, connection, temporary, dial tcp, too many requests, rate limit, service unavailable, bad gateway'. None matches 'Kafka write errors (1/1)' or 'topic partition has no leader', so RetryDisposition returns terminal for both.

platform/kafka/reply_delivery.go's own comment, which was true and named a caller that does not exist on this path: 'Transient: broker unreachable, context cancelled. Resending the same bytes may well work, so the caller's existing retry path stays in charge' - on the complete_workflow path the caller is failWorkflow, which has no retry.

The asymmetry this closes: notifyParentOfSuccess goes through kafka.DeliverReply (the bugs_open/133 shared seam) and converts an undeliverable success into notifyParentOfFailure, while notifyParentOfFailure's own send is a bare fire-once s.producer.Produce with a log-and-drop on error.

bugs_open/274, the reason deterministic errors are excluded and the third needle refused: 'A validation refusal is PERMANENT for this message: the headers are wrong by construction, so the same bytes can never pass on any retry (bugs_open/274 - this was classified transient and a deterministic defect spent 12 days being reported as "try again")'.

The duplicate-absorption premise, named rather than assumed: the parent's two-phase claim at coordinator.go ClaimAwaitedRequest, plus processed_messages (SYS-049). kafka-go v0.4.47 has no idempotent producer, so a retry after a lost ack CAN duplicate a reply and this is what absorbs it.

bugs_open/040 section 6's CORRECTION, which is why this is a separate round from the instrumentation: the council REJECTED round 1 because behaviour changes to shared messaging plumbing were 'bundled into what was presented as instrumentation ... argued from a remark in this file and from the Java client's defaults, NOT from measurement, while building the instrument that would have measured them'.

Owner ruling 2026-08-02 section 2: 'when a seam's widest branch is licensed by "callers must all be X", make X a field with the unsafe default OFF ... A comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share.' Hence WithRetry as an opt-in option adopted at four named call sites, rather than a retry inside Produce.
plan.risks: (1) DUPLICATE REPLIES are the real risk and cannot be prevented at this layer: kafka-go v0.4.47 has no idempotent producer, so a retry after a LOST ACK sends the reply twice. The premise is that the parent's two-phase ClaimAwaitedRequest and processed_messages absorb it - which is why the adopters are restricted to sites whose consumer is a parent orchestration with that dedupe, and why this is not a retry inside Produce where 39 call sites with unaudited consumers would inherit it. A reviewer should check that premise at each adopter, and the named disconfirming signal is DUPLICATE_SKIPPED volume rising after the roll. (2) LATENCY: worst case ~44s (4 attempts x the 10s WriteTimeout plus backoff) before a reply is finally reported undeliverable, holding the step for that long. Stated in the doc comment; the trade is against losing a completed workflow, which is what happens today. Not appropriate for a hot dispatch path, hence opt-in. (3) THE NEEDLES CHANGE WHAT RE-RUNS, which is the half that reaches beyond this file: after this, a child hitting either string may be redispatched by its parent rather than failing terminally. Redispatch is capped at retry_version >= 3 and the child re-runs from its start; head rows with no parent still terminate, and that residue is honest and stays in the bug file. (4) NEEDLE OVER-MATCH: 'no leader' is short. I checked it against the estate's error prose and found no other producer of that phrase, and 'write message to kafka' was refused precisely because it DOES over-match - a control test asserts the two deterministic refusals stay TERMINAL. If a reviewer knows of other 'no leader' prose, that is the objection to make. (5) TWO HONEST TESTING NOTES rather than claims: a test caught a real cap-breaking defect in my own jitter, and the default-OFF pin does not discriminate the cfg.retry flag (the zero policy's clamp covers it in series) - both recorded in the test file and the register entry rather than glossed. (6) DOES NOT CLOSE bugs_open/040: the timeout residual (146/7d) is undiagnosed and the refused mechanism is INFERRED.
